summary: Today’s pulse tracks Top Democrats slam ‘Trump’s failing economic agenda’ after weaker-than-expected jobs growth – US politics live, Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry was 'failed' by officials, says New York governor, and Riot police clash with students as education protests rage in France. Across Guardian and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are accused, black, and court. In the background, What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next and Olivia Dean accused of plagiarism on her I’ve Seen It track keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Top Democrats slam ‘Trump’s failing economic agenda’ after weaker-than-expected jobs growth – US politics live
headlines.description: Elizabeth Warren and Chuck Schumer criticize president after US added 29,000 new jobs in September, sharply less than the 84,000 economists had predicted Many indicators of voter sentiment suggest the Democrats are favored to take back control of the House of Representatives , and potentially the Senate. Winning either would be a significant victory for the party and give it the power to block Trump’s legislative agenda and more aggressively investigate his administration.

headlines.title: Woman at centre of Cornell rape inquiry was 'failed' by officials, says New York governor
headlines.description: The woman, known as Jane Doe, alleges she was raped by seven students at a fraternity house at the university in 2024.

headlines.title: Riot police clash with students as education protests rage in France
headlines.description: More than 600 schools have faced disruption as protests over standards and lack of teachers continue.

headlines.title: What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?
headlines.description: The convicted killer is in hospital in Tennessee after surviving two lethal injections, in a case that has raised many questions.

headlines.title: Olivia Dean accused of plagiarism on her I’ve Seen It track
headlines.description: Mattie Music Group, owners of Bill Withers’ back catalogue, contend the Grammy winner infringed on Just the Two of Us Olivia Dean has been accused of plagiarizing the Bill Withers classic Just the Two of Us. The owners of Withers’ back catalogue aimed that allegation at his fellow Grammy winner in a copyright infringement lawsuit filed on Thursday in US federal court in Los Angeles.

headlines.title: Palestine Action activists used whips and hammers to threaten guards at arms factory, court hears
headlines.description: Five defendants accused of being part of ‘black team’ tasked with overcoming security at Israel-linked firm Elbit near Bristol Palestine Action activists brandished whips, hammers and kebab skewers to intimidate security guards and keep them at bay during a break-in at an Israel-linked arms factory, a court has heard. Five defendants are accused by prosecutors of being part of a “black team”, wearing black jumpsuits, whose role was to overwhelm security guards, so that a “red team”, wearing red jumpsuits, could break into the Elbit systems factory in Filton, near Bristol, and smash up equipment including drones.

headlinePool.title: Burnham to pass law scrapping pension triple lock before next election
headlinePool.description: Guarantee will remain until 2030 but MPs will vote on changes during this parliament, government says Andy Burnham will pass legislation to scrap the state pension triple lock in this parliament, even though the guarantee will remain until 2030, the government has said. The prime minister used his conference speech to announce a change to the policy, which guarantees that the state pension rises by the highest of 2.5%, inflation or earnings growth.

headlinePool.title: Spanish right wing votes down housing crisis plans as protest movement grows
headlinePool.description: Opposition lawmakers join forces to defeat proposals made by Socialist-led coalition after eviction of 87-year-old Rightwing lawmakers in Spain have joined forces to reject emergency measures put forward to tackle the country’s housing crisis, pitting a fractured parliament against the widespread protest movement that has swelled in recent days. As protesters outside the parliament building in Madrid held up homemade signs bearing images of vultures, the conservative People’s party, the far-right Vox and the Catalan pro-independence party Junts voted against a package of decrees by Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist-led coalition that included a ban on evictions until 2030 and the regulation of temporary lettings and lettings by room.

headlinePool.title: Woman in alleged Cornell gang-rape case was ‘failed’ by system, New York governor says
headlinePool.description: Kathy Hochul briefs journalists with state attorney general Letitia James, who will be taking over the entire case Letitia James appointed special prosecutor in alleged gang-rape at Cornell Kathy Hochul, New York’s governor, said on Friday that she would “ensure” that all the facts of the alleged gang-rape at a fraternity house at Cornell University “are brought into the light”, while harshly criticizing the elite institution for how it handled the 2024 case. Hochul, a Democrat, said the woman in the case, was “failed” by people obligated to protect her, including the police and the county prosecutor.

headlinePool.title: Peter Thiel revealed as secret buyer of Bel Air mansion that sold for $130m
headlinePool.description: The 1938 mansion, Casa Encantada, once belonged to Conrad Hilton and was sold at foreclosure auction Tech billionaire Peter Thiel has been revealed as the new owner of a storied Bel-Air estate that quietly sold in July for a staggering $130m. The 1938 mansion, Casa Encantada, was sold at an open-air foreclosure auction in Pomona, with the name of the buyer kept under wraps for months. The winning bid is now revealed to have come from a limited liability company linked to the venture capitalist and PayPal and Palantir co-founder, according to the Wall Street Journal, which first reported the buyer’s identity .

headlinePool.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates
headlinePool.description: The diplomatic fallout comes as Ethiopian forces battle rebel fighters across its northern region.

headlinePool.title: England school inspections to be overhauled again after barrage of complaints
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Education secretary sends Ofsted back to ‘drawing board’ as teachers raise serious concerns about new system School inspections in England will be overhauled for the second time in a year, after a barrage of complaints that the new system was dangerously stressful and damaging teachers’ mental health. Lucy Powell, the education secretary, will tell the schools regulator Ofsted to “go back to the drawing board” after becoming concerned that inspection changes overseen by her predecessor, Bridget Phillipson, were creating problems for headteachers.

headlinePool.title: G7 to release up to 100m barrels of emergency oil and diesel reserves
headlinePool.description: Leaders agree a coordinated drawdown within four months as rising prices put pressure on households and economies Leaders of G7 nations are to release up to 100m barrels of their emergency diesel and crude oil stockpiles after coming under pressure from Donald Trump to ease surging fuel prices. The drawdown of reserves from some of the world’s largest economies will be coordinated by the International Energy Agency (IEA) and will take place within four months, according to France’s president, Emmanuel Macron.

headlinePool.title: Polanski says he does not need to win ‘50/50’ byelection to stay Green leader
headlinePool.description: Exclusive: Party leader says outcome of ‘knife-edge’ vote in Keir Starmer’s former seat will not affect his position Zack Polanski has said his authority as leader of the Green party of England and Wales does not depend on winning next week’s Holborn and St Pancras byelection, amid suggestions the party’s popularity may have peaked. Polanski, who is trying to take Keir Starmer’s former seat from Labour, described the contest as “probably 50/50 right now” and “really on a knife edge”.
